issues.issue: Whether the RAD had to defer to the RPD's credibility findings
issues.applicant_position: RAD owed deference to RPD credibility findings because the RPD saw the applicant testify in person.
issues.result_text: RAD was not required to show deference to the RPD's credibility findings.

issues.issue: Whether the RAD unreasonably found the presumption of truthfulness rebutted
issues.applicant_position: RAD did not give her the benefit of the presumption of truthfulness; her explanations for hiding Norwegian identity were reasonable.
issues.result_text: RAD reasonably found her false statements badly tainted her credibility and rebutted the presumption of truthfulness.

issues.issue: Whether the RAD unreasonably weighed the psychological evaluation
issues.applicant_position: Little weight to psychological report solely because the psychologist lacked firsthand knowledge was unreasonable.
issues.result_text: No reviewable error; the RAD's disagreement on weight of the psychological evaluation is not reviewable.

issues.issue: Whether the RAD unreasonably refused an oral hearing
issues.applicant_position: Psychological report was new evidence enhancing credibility, so an oral hearing was needed.
issues.result_text: RAD did not err in refusing an oral hearing; new evidence raised no new contradictions or issues.

issues.issue: Whether the RAD unreasonably assessed the risk of citizenship revocation and removal to Somalia
issues.applicant_position: Legal opinion confirms she will lose citizenship and removal to Somalia is not speculative.
issues.respondent_position: RAD considered the opinion; revocation is not automatic, enforcement is not persecution, and non-refoulement applies.
issues.result_text: Removal to Somalia is too remote to support Convention refugee protection; no reason to disturb the RAD's analysis.
